turns.text: Turn back to 20世纪中叶: Computationalism begins with “Computationalism understands cognition as inform” and asks us to rethink the relationship between machines, minds, and people.
Computationalism understands cognition as information processing or computation, using functional and program-like descriptions to ask whether machines can have minds.
The detail listeners may miss is “Computationalism”. Why does it become central to Computationalism?
The work or theory turns artificial making, autonomous action or computation into questions about agency, understanding and social order.
How should we assess Computationalism's influence and limits through the lens of “Computationalism”?
Researchers generally treat this node as an important cultural reference in AI humanities rather than a direct prediction of modern technology.
Starting from Computationalism, how should the next generation of AI handle the tension contained in “Computationalism”?
